concepts.title: Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam: The World as One Family
concepts.definition: The Hitopadesha verse that opens the chapter says the noble-minded count the whole world as one family, vasudhaiva kutumbakam; India has lived this ideal by welcoming peoples of many lands and faiths.
concepts.key_idea: Stranger-hood is a habit of small minds: India's civilisational habit has been to make newcomers its own.

concepts.title: Communities that Made India Home
concepts.definition: Over the centuries Jews, Christians, Zoroastrians, Muslims and others reached India's coasts and courts, fleeing persecution or seeking trade; each was allowed to worship, work and settle, and each enriched the land.
concepts.key_idea: Refugees became neighbours, and neighbours became Indians: acceptance turned arrival into belonging.

concepts.title: Acceptance as an Indian Value
concepts.definition: Acceptance is not mere tolerance: India's traditions taught that truth has many paths, so the newcomer's god, food and festival were given room beside one's own.
concepts.key_idea: Tolerance merely permits; acceptance honours: the deeper value made India a home rather than a camp.

concepts.title: How the Communities Enriched India
concepts.definition: The communities that made India home gave generously: Parsi enterprise built industry, Syrian Christian and Jewish traditions enriched trade and letters, Islamic art and cuisine reshaped tastes, and all joined the common chorus of India.
concepts.key_idea: Diversity is a treasury: every community that arrived left the country richer than it found it.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why do we say India was a home and not merely a destination for newcomers?

solution_template.explain: Each arriving community kept its faith and gained a secure place to live and work.
A destination is passed through; a home gives belonging, and India gave every community roots.
